chapter: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
title: Learning the club date business
summary: When things went bad he did weddings, bar mitzvahs and Italian and Polish jobs, booked every Wednesday at the union floor.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: About a year and a half, yeah. And then, let's see what happened after that. Oh, I started working around different little jobs and then things went bad and I started doin' the

club dates and I had to learn the Jewish music and the Italian music and doin' some Polish jobs. And usually I was the only colored man in the band, becuase I could entertain, but I had to learn that music and that was quite an experience. A lot of times Milton Hinton would be on the job, a lot of times Zoot Sims or Buck Clayton. We'd all be -- with our tuxedos -- doing a job. A wedding or a Barmitzvah or whatever. And I did that for a long time. And then we started doin' the parks in the Youth Program and I got pretty good into that club date business, which is another thing completely, you know.
I'm not really sure if I know just what that is like...

Well, what they do is you got a leader. He's got about--like a Saturday night--he's got about 15 or 20 bands workin' and he has a sub-leader who handles the job and he has the men and, if it's a wedding, you know, you play the wedding music. If it's a Barmitzvah,
you play the Barmitzvah music. If it's an Italian wedding, you know that music. Etcetera, etcetera. And it's strictly business.
How is it set up in terms of when do you find out, how do you find out what job you have at what time?
Well, we'd always meet on Wednesday on the union floor...

Yeah, that was headquarters. And all the guys met and all the contractors and leaders met and then they'd pick who they want and that was every Wednesday. And that's how we did this. It was like a clearing house, really. It was like sides of beef. (laughter)
